Two regressions found by unit probes of the fix's own functions; details in blocking:
- retryConstraints with a site rule.
- commandsIn on base vs fix.

blocking.issue: W15-25 drops whole critic findings from a research retry brief whenever their description (not only their required action) names a host the site rule refuses, or something that merely looks like a host. The retry then gets no findings at all, only the 'rule comes before any finding' line. This breaks design §4.6 (a retry brief carries the open findings). It is also wider than the spec, which says 'retryConstraints drops a required action naming a refused host'.
blocking.evidence:
Probe calling the branch's retryConstraints(2, findings, { refusesHost: webRuleRefuses({mode:'only', only:['developer.mozilla.org'], never:[]}) }). Two findings:
(1) description 'The free-tier figures for vercel.com and netlify.com have no source the run read: they come from memory.', required action 'Remove those figures or mark them as not verified under Uncertainty.'
(2) description 'The report says socket.io is required but the brief asks for plain WebSocket.', required action 'Drop socket.io from the recommendation.'
With the rule, the brief is only 'Attempt 3 (…)' and WEB_RULE_WINS_LINE: no 'Critic findings to resolve', both findings gone. Without the rule, both are listed. Neither required action asks to read a page. Finding 1 is exactly what W15-33's 'never from memory' planning leads the critic to raise. Under an only/never list the researcher retries blind, the critic sends it back again, and the ladder climbs to Opus and the person: the money pattern this wave fixes in W15-24. 'socket.io' (a library) counts as a host because 'io' is in HOST_TLD.
blocking.expected: Keep every finding in the retry brief. Drop, or replace with the rule line, only a required action that asks to read or fetch a page of a refused host. A finding whose action removes, marks or drops something stays as an order. Add a test with the probe's two findings that asserts both reach the brief under an 'only' rule. Keep the existing test for an order to fetch a refused page.

blocking.issue: W15-24's new CONNECTORS list makes many prose commands 'described' when they have no written argument, so they are no longer tried. This includes commands of tools that take no argument ('in a terminal', 'from the command line', 'to print', 'at the prompt') and bare runs said in words ('by itself', 'on its own'). No 'not tried' line replaces them for a script that does not read its command line. Verification that ran on the base silently stops (ADR 0104/0110 tries, rule 8 siblings).
blocking.where: packages/runtime/src/loop/try-plan.ts:140-145 (CONNECTORS), :379-386 (described when !kept.length), :210-211 (described skipped before commandTry), :226-238 (no notTried line unless READS_ARGS)
blocking.evidence:
commandsIn(text), base (claude/nifty-knuth-f9udt0) vs fix:
- 'Running node hello.js in a terminal prints Hello, world': base [node hello.js], fix []
- 'node hello.js from the command line prints Hello, world': base [node hello.js], fix []
- 'node greet.js to print a greeting': base [node greet.js], fix []
- 'node hello.js at the prompt prints the time': base [node hello.js], fix []
- 'node app.js by itself exits with code 1': base [node app.js], tried as a bare run that expects an error; fix []
The last one is the W15-24 pattern itself: a bare run that should expect an error. The fix handles only 'with no …' and 'without …'. No test covers these sentences.
blocking.expected: Treat a command as 'described' only when its arguments are really described: when the script reads its command line (READS_ARGS on its code) and nothing written is given. A tool that reads no arguments is run bare as before. Or narrow CONNECTORS to words that introduce an argument (on, with, against, using, given, passing) and handle 'by itself' / 'on its own' / 'alone' as bare runs. Add try-plan cases for a no-argument tool ('Running node hello.js from the command line prints Hello, world' is tried) and for 'node wc.js on its own exits with code 1' (tried bare, expects the error). Keep the live wc.js case passing.
